steps.title: Import TypeScript utilities for type safety
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript utilities 'keyof' and 'Record' that will be used to build type-safe i18n keys.
steps.hint: These are built-in TypeScript type operators, so you don't need to import them from a package. Just write a comment indicating you'll use them.
steps.seedCode:
// Import TypeScript utilities for type safety
// Use keyof and Record to create type-safe mappings
steps.expectedOutcome: A comment indicating you'll use TypeScript's keyof and Record utilities for type safety.
successCriteria: The code includes a comment mentioning both keyof and Record utilities.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've indicated the TypeScript utilities needed for type-safe i18n keys.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to mention both keyof and Record in your comment.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction: you need to write a comment about using keyof and Record utilities.

steps.title: Define the translation keys interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'TranslationKeys' that defines all possible translation keys as string literals. Use the 'keyof' operator to reference an object type containing your app's translation keys.
steps.hint: Start with 'interface TranslationKeys' and define properties using string literal types like 'welcome' or 'title'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that defines your translation keys as type-safe string literals.
successCriteria: The interface is named 'TranslationKeys' and contains at least one string literal property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a structured interface for translation keys, which is the foundation for type-safe lookups.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface is named 'TranslationKeys' and contains string literal properties like 'welcome' or 'title'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface is missing or incorrectly defined. Create an interface named 'TranslationKeys' with string literal properties.

steps.title: Define the translations interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named Translations that uses Record to map TranslationKeys to string values.
steps.hint: Use the Record utility type with TranslationKeys as the key type and string as the value type.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named Translations is defined that maps each translation key to a string value using Record<TranslationKeys, string>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a type-safe mapping interface that ensures each translation key corresponds to a string value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface uses Record with TranslationKeys as the key type and string as the value type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface should be named Translations and use Record<TranslationKeys, string> to create a type-safe mapping.

steps.title: Create the English translations object
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'englishTranslations' that contains English text for each key, ensuring it matches the structure of the Translations interface.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword to declare a variable. Assign it an object with properties that correspond to the keys in your TranslationKeys interface, each containing an English string.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a constant object containing English translations that TypeScript can verify against your interfaces.
successCriteria: The 'englishTranslations' constant is declared and contains English string values for each translation key.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed English translations object. This ensures your translations have the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your object includes all required keys from your TranslationKeys interface with English string values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The translations object doesn't match the expected structure. Check that you've declared a constant with the correct property names and English string values.

steps.title: Create the Spanish translations object
steps.instruction: Create a Spanish translations object named 'spanishTranslations' that conforms to the Translations interface.
steps.hint: Define a constant with the same structure as 'englishTranslations', but with Spanish text values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Spanish translations object is defined with the correct type annotation and Spanish text values.
successCriteria: The 'spanishTranslations' object is declared with the 'Translations' type and contains Spanish translations for all required keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a type-safe Spanish translations object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a Spanish object, but check that it's properly typed with the 'Translations' interface and contains all required keys.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Spanish translations object is missing or doesn't conform to the required structure. Make sure to define it with the 'Translations' type.

steps.title: Define the language type
steps.instruction: Create a union type named 'Language' that includes the string literals 'en' and 'es' to represent supported languages.
steps.hint: Use the TypeScript union type syntax with the pipe (|) operator to combine multiple string literal types.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a union type for status values
type Status = 'active' | 'inactive' | 'pending';
steps.expectedOutcome: A union type named Language is defined with 'en' and 'es' as its possible values.
successCriteria: The Language type is defined as a union of 'en' and 'es' string literals.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a union type for supported languages, which will help ensure type safety when selecting languages.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your type includes both 'en' and 'es' as string literals using the union syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Language type should be a union of string literals 'en' and 'es'. Try using the syntax: type Language = 'en' | 'es';

steps.title: Create the translations map
steps.instruction: Create a Record named 'translationsMap' that maps Language union type values to their corresponding translation objects. Use the English and Spanish translation objects you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Use Record<Language, Translations> as the type for your translationsMap. Assign the English object to 'en' and the Spanish object to 'es'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Record named translationsMap is created with type Record<Language, Translations>, containing the English and Spanish translation objects.
successCriteria: translationsMap is defined as a Record with Language keys and Translations values, with 'en' mapped to the English object and 'es' mapped to the Spanish object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a type-safe translations map that properly associates each language code with its translation object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that translationsMap has the correct type annotation (Record<Language, Translations>) and includes both language keys with their corresponding objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The translations map isn't quite right. Make sure to create a Record with Language keys and Translations values, assigning the English object to 'en' and Spanish object to 'es'.

steps.title: Create the type-safe lookup function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'translate' that takes a language and a key, and returns the corresponding translation string from the translations map.
steps.hint: Define a function with two parameters: 'lang' of type Language and 'key' of type keyof TranslationKeys. Inside, return the value from the translations map using both parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function that can retrieve translations in a type-safe way, ensuring the key exists and the language is valid.
successCriteria: The 'translate' function is defined with proper TypeScript types for its parameters and return value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your translate function correctly uses the Language type and TranslationKeys interface to ensure type safety.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function parameters are typed (lang: Language, key: keyof TranslationKeys) and it returns the correct translation from the map.
steps.feedbackWrong: The translate function is missing or has incorrect types. Review the function signature and ensure it matches the expected parameters and return type.

steps.title: Test the type-safe lookup with valid keys
steps.instruction: Create a test function named testTranslations that demonstrates using the translate function with valid keys from both English and Spanish languages.
steps.hint: Call the translate function multiple times with different valid keys and languages, then return the results in an array or log them.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test function that demonstrates type-safe access to translations using valid keys and languages.
successCriteria: The testTranslations function exists and calls the translate function with valid keys from both 'en' and 'es' languages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a test function that demonstrates type-safe translation lookups.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a test function, but it doesn't demonstrate translations from both languages or use valid keys.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test function is missing or doesn't properly demonstrate type-safe translation lookups.

steps.title: Demonstrate type safety with invalid keys
steps.instruction: Add a function call that attempts to use an invalid translation key to trigger a TypeScript error.
steps.hint: Call the translate function with a key that doesn't exist in your TranslationKeys interface, like 'invalidKey'.
steps.expectedOutcome: TypeScript will show a compile-time error when you try to use an invalid translation key, demonstrating the type safety of your i18n system.
successCriteria: The code includes a call to translate with a key that doesn't exist in TranslationKeys, triggering a TypeScript error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! TypeScript correctly prevents using invalid translation keys at compile time, showing how your type-safe i18n system protects against runtime errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling translate with a key that doesn't exist in your TranslationKeys interface to trigger the TypeScript error.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try calling the translate function with a key that isn't defined in your TranslationKeys interface, like 'invalidKey' or 'nonexistent'.

lessonTitle: Build type safe i18n key lookup
